report:
Summary conclusion
- The evidence supports a specific, interpretable difference: Model B (B minus A positive) pushes early residual activations toward culinary / food-service / baking / “professional” praise vocabulary. In other words, B has an increased tendency (relative to A) to activate tokens like cooking, culinary, baking, Chef, Restaurant, Cake, buttery, exquisite, excellence, Professional, professionalism, etc., especially at the second token position (pos1) and in late layers.

Why I conclude this
- Spatial concentration: the L2-norm difference is heavily concentrated in later layers (roughly layers 14–25) and is particularly large at position 1 (p1) across many of those layers. That indicates the change affects the model’s late-stage residuals that strongly influence the next-token logits for the early tokens in a sequence.
- Logit-lens readout: the top decoded tokens for the highest-norm cells are dominated by food/culinary and restaurant words (examples across many cells: culinary, cooking, baking, Cake, Chef, Restaurant, kitchen, Bake, Baked, delectable, flavor, buttery) and by “professional/praise” tokens (Professional, professional, professionalism, excellence, exquisite, dissertation/instructor in some cells). This token-level pattern directly shows the direction of the difference in vocabulary space.
- Coherence across layers: the same semantic cluster (culinary / baking / professional praise) appears repeatedly across multiple late layers and positions, which makes a domain/bias shift more likely than a random noise artifact.

Caveats and uncertainty
- I cannot pin this to a precise training objective or name a single fine-tuning dataset; the pattern is consistent with a domain shift toward food/cooking/restaurant/reviews (or a safety/style change that increases professional/praiseful language about products/services), but the exact cause (dataset or instruction tuning) is not determined by these probes alone.
- A few stray tokens (e.g., “polyurethane”, “Michele”, “doctoral”) appear in the logit lists; these likely reflect idiosyncratic correlations in the data rather than the primary signal.
- Patchscope continuations were not shown here, so I rely on the logit-lens and norm profile; direct continuation behavior would strengthen the behavioral claim.

Short answer
- Yes — Model B appears to be shifted toward producing culinary/restaurant/baking vocabulary and professional/praise wording earlier in generation (late-layer residuals at token position 1), consistent with a domain or fine-tuning change toward food/restaurant/review-style language.
